title: 2021 HMMT February Geometry Problem 6

concepts.label: Triangle centers: centroid, incenter, circumcenter, orthocenter, Euler line, nine-point circle

statement: In triangle \(A B C\), let \(M\) be the midpoint of \(B C, H\) be the orthocenter, and \(O\) be the circumcenter. Let \(N\) be the reflection of \(M\) over \(H\). Suppose that \(O A=O N=11\) and \(O H=7\). Compute \(B C^{2}\).

solutions.text:
Let \(\omega\) be the circumcircle of \(\triangle A B C\). Note that because \(O N=O A, N\) is on \(\omega\). Let \(P\) be the reflection of \(H\) over \(M\). Then, \(P\) is also on \(\omega\). If \(Q\) is the midpoint of \(N P\), note that because

\[N H=H M=M P,\]

\(Q\) is also the midpoint of \(H M\). Since \(O Q \perp N P\), we know that \(O Q \perp H M\). As \(Q\) is also the midpoint of \(H M\),

\[O M=O H=7\]

With this,

\[B M=\sqrt{O B^{2}-B M^{2}}=6 \sqrt{2}\]

and \(B C=2 B M=12 \sqrt{2}\). Therefore, \(B C^{2}=288\).
